market.summary: The KLCI bounced 0.4% to 1,651.17 on bargain hunting after Tuesday's break, but it closed back inside nothing: still below the 1,655 level it lost yesterday, below its 10-month average (1,699.9) and with more stocks falling than rising. Rakuten Trade expects a 1,640–1,670 range this week. The monthly trend rule still fails, so no buying. Wait for a close back above about 1,700.

notes: Run on Wed 30 Sep, 7pm, after the close (TradingView data for 1,134 Bursa stocks; 255 liquid). Volume trend = 10-day average ÷ 60-day average. The KLCI bounced 0.4% to 1,651.17 but is still below Tuesday's broken 1,655 support and its 10-month average, so the market check fails. Gamuda's buy trigger fired (+4.0% to 5.18 on 4.5× volume after record FY26 results and a RM61bn order book) — the second trigger after Southern Cable, which held its breakout at 2.93. Neither can be bought until the market check passes; don't chase, wait for pullbacks toward the triggers. UMS traded again (+1.2%, new 1-month high 8.95 intraday), so its trigger moves up to 8.96. Powerwell bounced 3.5% to near its high. MN Holdings is stalling on thin volume. The solar installers pulled back 3–5% and Hengyuan fell 18% on profit-taking — watch the 'already ran' zones. The scheduled 6:20pm run did not happen today because the computer was not reachable at that time; this report was run manually.

catalysts.title: First CRESS data-centre deal signed — more to follow
catalysts.when: Signed 28 Sep; more expected over Q4 2026
catalysts.theme: Solar / green power for data centres
catalysts.detail: A JV of SD Guthrie (33.5%), Gamuda (33%) and Gentari (33.5%) signed a 21-year CRESS term sheet with a US tech company for at least 680MW of solar plus 4-hour battery storage in Perak, worth over RM10bn of revenue, running from 2029. It confirms the 30% green-power rule is turning into real contracts. HLIB expects Solarvest and Samaiden to sign their first CRESS projects within three months. The installers have already run; the supply chain (cables, switchgear, substations) and the asset owners have not moved as much.

catalysts.title: Gamuda: record FY2026 results and RM61bn order book
catalysts.detail: Gamuda reported a record FY2026 core profit of RM1.05bn (+5–6%) on revenue of RM18.6bn (+14%), and a record RM61bn order book after over RM12bn of new jobs in the first two months of FY27. Management targets construction revenue of RM24bn in FY27. Brokers kept Buy calls: HLIB RM5.75, MBSB RM5.60, CIMB RM6.10, RHB RM6.20. The share rose 4.0% to 5.18 on 4.5× normal volume.
beneficiaries: Its subcontractors and suppliers: Southern Cable, Kelington

catalysts.detail: US 10-year Treasury yields near a 19-year high and West Asia tensions keep the KLCI under pressure. Refiners, which had doubled, are now reversing: Hengyuan fell 18% today on heavy profit-taking and Bursa suspended intraday short selling in it. A fall in yields or a Hormuz de-escalation would be the trigger for a broader rebound.
beneficiaries: Negative for: banks, transport, consumer; refiners unwinding
